title: Street Talk: Asset consultant JANA fields M&A approach
full_text:
JANA Investment Advisers, one of the country's most influential investment consultants with clients such as Australian Retirement Trust and Hostplus, is in discussions to sell itself to an overseas suitor.
The 39-year-old business is negotiating a sale to London-based consultant Lane Clark & Peacock, people briefed on the matter said on the condition of anonymity. The two have been in discussions for months and are aiming to sign a deal by October, which comes about three years after JANA's management bought back Insignia Financial's stake in the business.
Should the deal proceed, private equity-backed Lane Clark & Peacock would take ownership of a business which advises on about $1.8 trillion of assets and has some of the country's largest superannuation funds and insurers on its books.
JANA and industry super-owned rival Frontier Advisors are the two best-known asset consultants in the $4.5 trillion superannuation sector, acting as gatekeepers for fund managers hoping to win pension money for their strategies. Both firms have also supplied plenty of C-suite talent to super funds, with former JANA chief executive Ian Patrick holding the chief investment officer position at Australian Retirement Trust.
However, a wave of consolidation among superannuation funds means JANA has sought to diversify its client book to include financial planning networks such as Stanford Brown and family offices such as Perron Group. Other players in the sector include Willis Towers Watson and Russell, and recent entrants like Evidentia have focused on financial planners.
JANA increased revenue 5.4 per cent to $66 million in the year ending September last year, according to accounts filed with the Australian Securities and Investment Commission. That boiled down to $9.8 million after-tax profit, the filings show.
JANA, which started life as John Anthony Nolan & Associates in 1987, was sold to National Australia Bank at the turn of the century. Its management bought back 55 per cent of the business from NAB in 2017.
Six years later, JANA's investment boffins acquired the remaining 45 per cent stake from Insignia, which had inherited the JANA stake via its 2021 acquisition of NAB's MLC Wealth. ASIC records show about 98 investors, including 4.6 per cent held by its chief executive Georgina Dudley.
Lane Clark & Peacock, founded 79 years ago, is best known for providing actuarial services, investment consulting and risk solutions to pension funds and insurers. However, it is also expanding into consulting services for energy transition, health and sports analytics. It reported £254 million ($481 million) in gross fees for the last financial year, rising from £232 million the year prior.
Its private equity backer, London's Charterhouse Capital Partners, appointed Rothschild in May as it considered selling its minority stake in the company, according to M&A Insights.
Spokespeople for JANA and Lane Clark & Peacock declined to comment.
